nodes.title: Introduction
widgets_values:
## Raylight Overview

As the name implies, **Raylight** uses Ray workers, called *Actors*.  
Each worker is its own Python process. While this allows splitting across multiple VRAMs,  
it does increase overall RAM usage.  

That said, RAM is generally much cheaper than VRAM, so this trade-off is acceptable in most cases.  

---

## More info: 

### [Raylight on GitHub](https://github.com/komikndr/raylight)
### [Raylight guide on Youtube](https://youtu.be/KQxrkJAV4eI?si=hAFY1rKD6Y2UHXqY)


## Supported Models

| Model               | USP | FSDP | CFG |
|---------------------|-----|------|-----|
| Wan2.X 14B T2V      | ✅  | ✅   | ✅  |
| Wan2.X 14B I2V      | ✅  | ✅   | ✅  |
| Wan2.1 1.3B T2V     | ✅  | ✅   | ✅  |
| Wan2.2 5B TI2V      | ✅  | ✅   | ✅  |
| Flux Dev            | ✅  | ✅   | ❌  |
| Flux Konteks        | ✅  | ✅   | ❌  |
| Flux Krea           | ✅  | ✅   | ❌  |
| Flux 2              | ✅  | ✅   | ❌  |
| Chroma              | ✅  | ✅   | ✅  |
| Chroma Radiance     | ✅  | ✅   | ✅  |
| Qwen Image/Edit     | ✅  | ✅   | ✅  |
| Z Image             | ✅  | ✅   | ✅  |
| Lumina 2            | ✅  | ✅   | ✅  |
| Hunyuan Video       | ✅  | ❌   | ❌  |
| Hunyuan 1.5         | ✅  | ❌   | ❌  |
| SD1.5 (UNet)        | ❌  | ❌   | ✅  |
| SDXL (UNet)         | ❌  | ❌   | ✅  |

**Legend:**
- ✅ = Supported  
- ❌ = Not supported  

**Notes:**
- Non standard Wan variant (Phantom, S2V, etc...) is not tested

## Scaled vs Non-Scaled Models

| Model       | USP | FSDP |
|-------------|-----|------|
| Non-Scaled  | ✅  | ✅   |
| Scaled      | ✅  | ⚠️ |

**Notes:**
- Scaled models use multiple dtypes inside their transformer blocks: typically **FP32** for scale, **FP16** for bias, and **FP8** for weights.
- Only Ada Lovelace and newer GPUs support **FP8 scaled FSDP2**.

nodes.title: LTX-2.5 on Raylight
widgets_values:
## LTX-2.5 on Raylight (GGUF)

**Models**
- `unet/ltx-2.5-22b-distilled-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf` (14 GB) from [unsloth/LTX-2.5-GGUF](https://huggingface.co/unsloth/LTX-2.5-GGUF) (`distilled/`); other quants work the same.
- From [Lightricks/LTX-2.5](https://huggingface.co/Lightricks/LTX-2.5) (accept the license there first):
  - `text_encoders/gemma4-12b-with-proj-ltx-2.5-comfy-int8-convrot.safetensors`
  - `vae/ltx-2.5-video-vae-bf16.safetensors`, `vae/ltx-2.5-audio-vae-bf16.safetensors`
  - `latent_upscale_models/ltx-2.5-latent-spatial-upscaler-x2-bf16-1.0.safetensors`
- Prompt enhancer: `text_encoders/gemma4_e2b_it_int8_convrot.safetensors` from [Comfy-Org/gemma-4](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/gemma-4). Set *Enable Prompt Enhance* to false to skip it.

**Input image**: [neon_cyborg_portrait.png](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Comfy-Org/workflow_templates/refs/heads/main/input/neon_cyborg_portrait.png)

Same graph and settings as ComfyUI's *LTX-2.5 Image to Video* template; the transformer runs on the Ray workers.

nodes.title: Parallelism
widgets_values:
A GGUF model runs with USP or CFG parallel, not FSDP: every GPU holds the whole model. On 12 GB
cards ComfyUI keeps part of it in system RAM; if sampling runs out of memory, start ComfyUI with --reserve-vram 3 (the
Ray workers use the same setting).

The distilled model samples at cfg 1 (video_cfg = audio_cfg = 1), so USP (ulysses_degree) is what speeds it up. CFG
parallel (cfg_degree 2) needs cfg > 1, as with the dev model.

Sampling time on 2x RTX 3060 12 GB with this GGUF:
- 1280x704, 121 frames (the second stage): 92.5 s on one GPU, 68.4 s with USP.
- 512x320, 97 frames: 57.2 s against 56.8 s. Every GPU streams the part of the model that does not fit in its
  VRAM in full, which outweighs its share of a small video.
- 512x320, dual CFG 3 / 7: 84.0 s on one GPU, 64.1 s with CFG parallel.

LTXV Spatio-Temporal Guidance (Ray), LTXV Modality Guidance (Ray) and LTXV Reference Audio (Ray) go between the loader
and the guiders, like their ComfyUI versions.
